tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Use it even if only the symptom is described'), focuses on observable symptoms/user intent (connection errors, timeouts, alarms firing) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts (error reply types, metrics, failover, etc.), and also explicitly states what is out of scope. It is a dense but bounded paragraph appropriate for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an application that uses an Amazon ElastiCache cache (node-based or serverless; Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) sees connection errors or timeouts, command errors or timeouts... Use it even if only the symptom is described. Do not use it to create, size or migrate caches, or for self-managed Valkey or Redis (for example on EC2).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific rules, conditions, and procedures specific to ElastiCache incident analysis. It avoids explaining generic concepts (e.g., it doesn't explain what CloudWatch or caching is) and jumps straight to non-obvious rules (G1-G4) and workflow specifics.
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent. That is CurrItems, CurrVolatileItems, latency percentiles, ReplicationLag...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (metric queries, error mappings, mitigation tables) is kept in references/ files and only linked/summarized in the body; no large reference tables or lookup data are embedded inline.
tests.evidence: Load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body (discover-deployment.md, query-otel-metrics.md, query-classic-metrics.md, check-events-and-changes.md, read-parameters.md, query-logs.md, error-replies.md, recommend-engine-command.md, propose-mitigation.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is attached to a specific condition or trigger for when to load it, e.g., tied to engine error replies, deployment discovery, or mitigation application.
tests.evidence: When the operator quotes an engine error reply, or the error metrics show one, load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use the relative 'references/filename.md' format from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (mitigation application, read-only investigation rules) are highly prescriptive with exact sequences, while judgment-heavy tasks (judging causes, evidence weighing) are described with reasoning and flexibility rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: Apply a change only when the operator asks you in chat to apply a mitigation and the change is a directed action they approve. Then follow Step 6.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple metric paths exist (OpenTelemetry vs classic), the skill gives clear rules for when to use each rather than presenting them as interchangeable equal options.
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent... For node-based Valkey, query both paths.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable method for root-causing any ElastiCache incident (identify deployment, collect evidence, judge causes, validate, report, mitigate) rather than a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Mark each cause confirmed (all its evidence is present), ruled out (its deciding evidence is absent) or unknown (evidence missing; name the gap).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes concrete, non-obvious domain gotchas as numbered rules (G1-G4) covering metric equivalence gaps, data loss risk, safe commands, and capacity change pitfalls.
tests.evidence: G4: never recommend a capacity change (a larger node, more shards or replicas, higher serverless limits) for a hot key, an unbounded collection or a client-side cause.
